chunks: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when he would go to his bed, would say:
In Your Name, O Allah, I live, and in Your Name, I die.
And when he would wake up, he would say:
All praise is due to Allah, who gave me life after He caused me to die,
and to Him is the resurrection.

key_terms.أَحْيَا: I live; affirming life through Allah’s power.
key_terms.أَحْيَانِي: He gave me life; referring to being restored from sleep.
key_terms.أَمَاتَنِي: He caused me to die; referring here to sleep as a likeness of death.
key_terms.أَمُوتُ: I die; acknowledging death as under Allah’s authority.
key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah; a direct form of supplication and calling upon Allah.
key_terms.النُّشُورُ: Resurrection; the return and rising to Allah after death.
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ: All praise; gratitude and praise directed to Allah upon waking.
key_terms.بِاسْمِكَ: By Your Name; invoking Allah at the moment of sleeping and waking.

ai.seo_question: What did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say before sleeping and after waking up?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the supplication recited at sleep and upon waking, expressing complete reliance upon Allah in life, death, and return. It frames sleep as a likeness of death and awakening as a reminder of resurrection, combining dhikr, gratitude, and awareness of the afterlife.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1387 - When the Messenger of Allah (sw) would go to his bed, he would say:

Bismika Allahumma ahya wa bismika amoot
"In Your name, O’ Allah (swt), I live, and in Your name, I die."
And when he would wake up, he would say:

Alhamdulillahi alladhi ahyayani ba‘da ma amatani wa ilayhi an-nushoor
"All praise is due to Allah (swt), who brought me back to life after causing me to die, and to Him is the return."
